 'Dignity and courtesy took a fall': India GM Srinath Narayanan criticises Magnus Carlsen over controversial forfeit 
 Trending Arin Ahuja India Vs New Zealand Australia Cricket Team Saurav Rathi Vivaan Kapoor Indian Lawn Bowlers Amandeep Johl Mohammad Nabi Son Vaibhav Sooryavanshi All India Football Federation Arin Ahuja India Vs New Zealand Australia Cricket Team Saurav Rathi Vivaan Kapoor Indian Lawn Bowlers Amandeep Johl Mohammad Nabi Son Vaibhav Sooryavanshi All India Football Federation Arin Ahuja India Vs New Zealand Australia Cricket Team Saurav Rathi Vivaan Kapoor Indian Lawn Bowlers Amandeep Johl Mohammad Nabi Son Vaibhav Sooryavanshi All India Football Federation 'Dignity and courtesy took a fall': India GM Srinath Narayanan criticises Magnus Carlsen over controversial forfeit 
 Edited by Jyotirmoy Halder / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 18, 2026, 16:59 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print Magnus Carlsen vs Bibisara Assaubayeva (Photo by Michal Walusza for Total Chess) NEW DELHI: Magnus Carlsen found himself in fresh controversy at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest on after deciding against playing his Fast Classic game against Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva on Tuesday. The Norwegian grandmaster forfeited the match after taking an unassailable lead through blitz and rapid games in the match, arguing that the remaining contest had no purpose once the day's result was decided. His decision drew criticism from Indian Grandmaster Srinath Narayanan , who questioned the lack of sportsmanship and respect shown by the former world champion. Watch Harika Dronavalli Exclusive: Inside Grenke #chess win, viral no-handshake incident, and more Carlsen had won three blitz games and drawn one before winning both rapid games, giving him an 11.5-0.5 lead. Since Assaubayeva could no longer surpass him even with a win, Carlsen decided not to turn up for the Fast Classic game. She was awarded the win by forfeit, making the final score 11.5-8.5 in Carlsen's favour. Srinath Narayanan criticises Carlsen 
 Reacting to the incident, Srinath, who coached and captained India's medal-winning teams at the Chess Olympiad, criticised Carlsen's conduct, writing on X, "Dignity and courtesy took a fall long before the rating." FIDE Enterprises CEO and Grandmaster Emil Sutovsky also expressed his displeasure, saying, "Hard to comment on such a pathetic unsporsmanlike conduct." Carlsen, however, defended his decision while speaking to Norwegian broadcaster TV2, arguing that there was little reason to play a game that could no longer affect the day's outcome. “The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally useless game,” he said. He added that he would understand the need to play if the match counted towards championship points and ratings. Carlsen's decision also came after a disappointing group-stage campaign in the Fast Classic format. He failed to win any of his 10 games, drawing nine and losing one. The results cost him 21.8 Elo points, bringing his live classical rating down to 2801.2 and putting his position as world No. 1 under pressure from Fabiano Caruana. Join conversation

Notably, a draw against Assaubayeva would have cost Carlsen 3.5 rating points, while a defeat would have resulted in an 8.5-point loss. However, the forfeited game did not affect either player's classical rating under FIDE rules.
